svg.text: Deep dive 3 — surges + high availability outside matching
ride-request queue = admission control, not storage · partition it by region · split the whole stack by data center
Ride requests
NYE · stadium · concert
Ride request queue
partitioned by REGION
· Manhattan
· DT Brooklyn
· … (fine-grained)
head-of-line guard: a hard match in
the boonies can't block NYC rides
Ride Matching services (n instances)
poll the queue · each match takes ~10 s of waiting —
expensive, long-running, the most likely thing to die
crash mid-match? it wasn't acked → pull it off again
surge drained
at steady pace
The queue is what makes the system surge-proof:
hundreds of thousands of requests stack up instead of
hitting the matchers all at once — and if a matcher
crashes, the message is re-delivered, not lost.
High availability OUTSIDE matching — the boring, reliable parts
· every service horizontally scaled behind its own load balancer — no single instance is precious
· stores chosen to scale: DynamoDB (nearly unbounded), Redis cluster (100k–1M ops/s) — both handle growth
· care about availability everywhere EXCEPT matching; matching trades availability for exactness (lock + TTL)
· travelers crossing regions: one read replica of the primary DB per data center — a user is always local
Split by region, in different data centers:
copy the whole stack → Northeast / Southwest / Northwest …
Why it helps you personally on the board:
less cross-node traffic, smaller queues, bounded blast radius.
